data.gender_notes: Azab is used as a male name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: In the Quran, the name Azab refers to a severe punishment or torment inflicted by Allah upon the disbelievers. The name Azab carries the meaning “Harsh Punishment” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Persian. Parents who choose Azab usually hope their child will grow to embody harsh punishment and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Reminder of the consequences of disbelief and the importance of faith.
data.etymology: Azab belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Harsh Punishment.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Azab total 3, giving a life-path number of 3. Number 3 is linked with Jupiter and with the qualities of creativity, expression and optimism.

in_arabic.name: عذاب
in_arabic.meaning: عذاب کا مطلب ہے تکلیف، اذیتی، یا سزا
in_arabic.long_meaning: عذاب (ʿadhāb) کا لفظ عربی زبان میں استعمال ہوتا ہے جس کا مطلب ہے تکلیف، اذیتی، یا سزا۔ یہ لفظ قرآن کریم میں بھی استعمال ہوا ہے، خاص طور پر ان لوگوں کے لئے جو اللہ کے احکام کی مخالفت کرتے ہیں۔ اس کا عربی جڑ 'ع ذ ب' (ʿ-dh-b) ہے جس کا تعلق درد یا تکلیف سے ہے۔ اسلامی تقویم میں، عذاب کا ذکر اکثر ان لوگوں کے لئے ہوتا ہے جو دنیا میں بد عمل کرتے ہیں اور آخرت میں سزا پاتے ہیں۔

in_urdu.name: عذاب
in_urdu.meaning: عذاب کا مطلب تکلیف، سزا یا اذیت ہے
in_urdu.long_meaning: عذاب (ʿadhāb) کا لفظ عربی سے ماخوذ ہے اور اردو میں بھی اسی معنی میں استعمال ہوتا ہے۔ یہ تکلیف، سزا، یا اذیت کے لئے استعمال ہوتا ہے۔ قرآن کریم میں عذاب کا ذکر ان لوگوں کے لئے ہوا ہے جو اللہ کے احکام کی مخالفت کرتے ہیں۔ عذاب کی اصطلاح تاریخی اور روحانی سیاق و سباق میں اہم ہے، خاص طور پر جنوبی ایشیائی اسلامی روایت میں جہاں اسلامی اقدار اور تعلیمات پر زور دیا جاتا ہے۔

in_hindi.name: عذاب
in_hindi.meaning: عذاب का अर्थ है तकलीफ, सजा या अज़ाब
in_hindi.long_meaning: عذاب (ʿadhāb) का शब्द अरबी मूल से है और हिंदी में भी इसी अर्थ में प्रयोग किया जाता है। यह तकलीफ, सजा, या अज़ाब के लिए प्रयोग होता है। कुरआन में عذاب का उल्लेख उन लोगों के लिए हुआ है जो अल्लाह के आदेशों का उल्लंघन करते हैं। عذاب की शब्दावली भारतीय मुस्लिम समुदाय में ऐतिहासिक और आध्यात्मिक संदर्भ में महत्वपूर्ण है, जहाँ इस्लामी मूल्यों और शिक्षाओं पर बल दिया जाता है।

in_pashto.name: عذاب
in_pashto.meaning: عذاب د تکلیف، سزا یا اذیت معنی
in_pashto.long_meaning: عذاب (ʿadhāb) د عربی کلمې څخه اخیستل شوی دی او په پښتو کې هم په همدې معنا کارول کیږي. دا تکلیف، سزا، یا اذیت لپاره کارول کیږي. په قرآن کریم کې عذاب د هغو کسانو لپاره یاد شوی دی چې د الله تعالی حکمونه یې مخالفت کړي. عذاب اصطلاح په افغان او پښتني دودیزو سیاقاتونو کې مهم دی، چیرته چې د اسلامي ارزښتونو او تعلیماتو ټینګار کیږي.

in_english.name: Azab
in_english.meaning: Azab means torment, punishment, or affliction
in_english.long_meaning: The term Azab (ʿadhāb) originates from Arabic and is used in Islamic contexts to denote torment, punishment, or affliction. It is mentioned in the Quran as a consequence for those who disobey God's commands. Etymologically, it stems from the Arabic root 'ʿ-dh-b' which relates to pain or distress. Historically and spiritually, Azab holds significance in Islamic tradition as a reminder of the consequences of disbelief and misdeeds. In contemporary Muslim cultures, the name Azab serves as a reminder of the importance of righteousness and adherence to Islamic teachings.

pronunciation.pashto: په پښتو کې د تلفظ تفصیل: عذاب

data.spiritual_significance: From a spiritual perspective, the name Azab highlights the importance of faith, obedience, and submission to Allah. It is a reminder of the balance between Allah's mercy and His justice, and serves as a warning against straying from the path of righteousness. Additionally, it reminds us of the need to seek Allah's forgiveness and avoid actions that could incur His wrath and punishment. Ultimately, the name Azab inspires reverence for Allah's power and sovereignty, and encourages us to strive towards living a virtuous and obedient life.

historical_references.reference: The Battle of Uhud (625 AD) marked a significant turning point in the Islamic history and resulted in the defeat of the Muslim army led by Muhammad (PBUH). The term Azab refers to the severe punishment inflicted upon the Muslims following this defeat. The men, women and children were subjected to various forms of torment, including the cutting off of hands and feet, crucifixion, and the burning of houses.
historical_references.context: Immediately after the Battle of Uhud

historical_references.reference: The term Azab also appears in the context of the Prophet Moses (AS) in the Quran, where it refers to a punishment inflicted upon the people of Pharaoh for their disobedience. The punishment was a series of torments and trials, including the sending of various plagues and the drowning of the Pharaoh's army in the Red Sea.
historical_references.context: In the context of the Prophet Moses (AS) and the people of Pharaoh

In modern times, this term has gained popularity among certain Islamic communities, particularly those with apocalyptic beliefs and a focus on end times. On social media platforms, there are numerous groups and pages dedicated to discussing the meaning and significance of 'Azab'.
